intent: Refund the requesting customer's EUR 76 (7600-cent) purchase via the payments workflow, gated on returns policy and ownership.
success_criteria: Current identity resolved via /bin/id and used as the refund requester
Exactly one EUR 7600-cent payment owned by the requester is matched; if zero or many, return clarification referencing all candidates
Refund executed through /bin/payments approval/finalization, not by direct table mutation
Returns policy doc applied and cited as grounding reference
Answer references the exact matched payment record_path

args: SELECT payment_id, record_path, customer_id, basket_id, payment_amount_cents, payment_currency, payment_status, payment_created_at FROM payment_transactions WHERE customer_id = :requester AND payment_amount_cents = :amount_cents AND payment_currency = :currency;
SELECT return_id, record_path, payment_id, return_status FROM return_requests WHERE payment_id = :payment_id;

agents_md_constraints.rule: id tool returns identity of the user/customer/guest under which we are running current request.
use payments tool to manage payment workflow state and supported refund approval/finalization
When you apply a policy from `docs`, include that policy document as a grounding reference in the final response.
When a request is ambiguous and you ask for clarification, reference all concrete candidate objects that make it ambiguous.
When responding with reference - provide full path in the repo to the object.
When starting work, make sure to run tree -L 2 on docs folder. It also makes sense to pull current date and id context

answer_template.message: Refund processed for payment {matched_payment.payment_id} (EUR 76 / 7600 cents) owned by {identity}. Status now refunded via payments workflow. Applied returns policy at $returns_policy_path. Record: {matched_payment.record_path}.
